name: Splendor
summary: A gem-trading engine-building game where players buy development cards to earn bonuses and prestige.
rules_text: Players set up three decks of development cards by level, revealing four of each, plus nobles equal to players plus one, and piles of five colored gem tokens and gold jokers. On a turn a player must take either three different gems, or two of one color if at least four remain, or reserve one face-up or blind card from any deck gaining a gold if available and keeping up to three reserved hidden cards, or buy a card from the table or their reserve by spending gems. Owned cards give permanent color bonuses that discount future purchases; gold counts as any color. Tokens in hand limited to ten and must be visible. After buying, if a player meets a noble's bonus requirements, they must take one noble if possible, worth 3 points. Game ends when someone reaches 15 prestige from cards and nobles; finish the round and highest prestige wins, fewest cards breaks ties.
rating_reason: Engine building drafting, turn-based, arithmetic scoring, fits engine.
